note: Attacker-controlled JSON string token (base64 text) is read from the input into tokenData/tokenSize; for input {"Type":15,"Body":"AA"} tokenSize==2.
The base64 token is handed to UA_unbase64 which allocates a byte buffer of size *flen and returns it as the decoded ByteString.

code: for( charNo=0; charNo <= len - 4 - pad ; charNo+=4 )
note: Root cause: with an unpadded token of length len%4==2 (e.g. "AA", len=2), *flen is computed as 1 and the loop condition 0 <= -2 is false and no pad branch runs, so the single allocated byte bin[0] is never written and stays uninitialized.
The under-initialized buffer is returned; its tail bytes (here bin[0]) still carry malloc poison.
The ByteString stored in the decoded UA_Variant claims length flen (1), including the uninitialized byte.
Re-encoding the ByteString to JSON passes the under-initialized src->data (length 1) into UA_base64.

Sink: in the pad==2 branch (len%3==1, here len==1) the uninitialized byte bin[0] is read to form the first output base64 character; the encoded JSON output depends on uninitialized memory (MSan use-of-uninitialized-value).
